title: After the RAF Fairford incident, the UK should develop its homeland defence forces
gist: Chatham House argues the UK, after the RAF Fairford plot and US bomber withdrawal, needs dedicated locally recruited home-defence reserve units modeled on Poland, plus Finland-style permanent funded planning.

insights.claim: The US withdrew its bombers from RAF Fairford after a suspected terror plot and the arrest of five men near the base on 27 September, with PM Andy Burnham citing strong indications Iran played a part, which Iran denies.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: UK bases hosting US operations against Iran are now viewed as targets, raising UK security risk.

insights.claim: Iran warned any base used for aggression against Iranian territory would be a legitimate target, after the UK approved US use of Fairford for defensive strikes in March.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Permitting allied operations from UK soil creates retaliation exposure.

insights.claim: Russia poses a major hybrid threat, and Danish intelligence has warned it could mount a limited attack on a NATO member within months.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Raises European defence and infrastructure security demand.

insights.claim: The UK lacks a specialist domestic-only force able to protect a wide range of sites for a long period, and relying on the same reservists for home and NATO deployment fails when both demands coincide.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Expect pressure for new home-defence force spending.

insights.claim: A January University of Exeter report found UK home defence is fragmented with no lead department holding executive tasking authority, leaving the UK at a standing start versus Finland, Poland and the Baltics.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: A designated lead department is a likely first policy step.

insights.claim: British Army major exercises were reportedly suspended this year for lack of funds and reservists are set to serve fewer days due to budget cuts, showing training budgets are vulnerable.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Squeezed defence budgets undermine readiness; argues for ring-fenced homeland funding.
insights.locator: Three changes the UK should make

insights.claim: The UK should create locally recruited reserve sub-units with a purely domestic protective role near key bases and critical infrastructure, not counted as reinforcements for overseas deployment and able to hold sites for months.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Potential new defence procurement and manpower spending.
insights.locator: Three changes the UK should make

insights.claim: Poland's Territorial Defence Force, established in 2017 as a fifth service branch, is organized by province and tasked with protecting critical infrastructure; Finland treats homeland protection as a permanent cross-government function.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Reference models for European homeland-defence design.

insights.claim: When the government permits an operation from British territory it should decide protective requirements for the site at the same time.
insights.speaker: Chatham House
insights.so_what: Links allied basing decisions to protection spending.
